authorityBoundary: Role assignment, RACI, and demonstrated competence do not appoint a person or grant recommendation, acceptance, risk, implementation, repository, release, operational, assurance, or audit authority.

raciLegend.R: Responsible — performs or coordinates the bounded work.
raciLegend.A: Accountable — exactly one named role/body owns the bounded governed decision.
raciLegend.C: Consulted — provides required knowledge before the decision.
raciLegend.I: Informed — receives the decision and material effects.

raciRules: Every governed decision has exactly one accountable role or explicitly named accountable governance body.
Missing accountability blocks acceptance and commit for the affected decision.
Product Owner is never a universal default; accountability follows the decision domain.
Independent assurance cannot be performed by the same bounded actor whose work is being independently assured.
RACI does not imply organizational authority or competence.

roleArchetypes.label: Governing body
roleArchetypes.scope: Sets enterprise direction and reserved decision rights.

roleArchetypes.label: Executive sponsor
roleArchetypes.scope: Sponsors bounded adoption and resolves executive dependencies.

roleArchetypes.label: Product leadership
roleArchetypes.scope: Owns portfolio/product policy and product-level tradeoffs.

roleArchetypes.label: Product Manager
roleArchetypes.scope: Leads evidence-based Product discovery, outcomes, and roadmap proposals.

roleArchetypes.label: Product Owner
roleArchetypes.scope: Performs legitimate team/backlog Product Owner work where the organization assigns it; not a universal governor.

roleArchetypes.label: Initiative lead
roleArchetypes.scope: Coordinates the bounded Initiative and unresolved dependencies.

roleArchetypes.label: Business owner
roleArchetypes.scope: Owns bounded business outcomes and business acceptance decisions.

roleArchetypes.label: Domain expert
roleArchetypes.scope: Provides domain language, rules, evidence, and challenge.

roleArchetypes.label: Business architect
roleArchetypes.scope: Models capabilities, value streams, operating model, and business boundaries.

roleArchetypes.label: Enterprise architect
roleArchetypes.scope: Owns enterprise architecture coherence and architecture decision policy.

roleArchetypes.label: Solution architect
roleArchetypes.scope: Designs and challenges solution/integration/deployment architecture for the affected slice.

roleArchetypes.label: Data/AI architect
roleArchetypes.scope: Owns data and AI architecture reasoning, model/provider constraints, and lifecycle risks.

roleArchetypes.label: Security architect
roleArchetypes.scope: Leads threat-informed security architecture and evidence requirements.

roleArchetypes.label: Privacy specialist
roleArchetypes.scope: Leads privacy impact, data-use, rights, and minimization analysis.

roleArchetypes.label: Legal/regulatory specialist
roleArchetypes.scope: Interprets applicable legal/regulatory obligations within authorized practice.

roleArchetypes.label: Risk/compliance specialist
roleArchetypes.scope: Assesses applicability, control outcomes, residual risk, and compliance evidence without granting risk acceptance.

roleArchetypes.label: User research and Product Design
roleArchetypes.scope: Produces and evaluates tool-neutral Product Design and user evidence.

roleArchetypes.label: Engineering leadership
roleArchetypes.scope: Owns engineering execution policy, implementation authority, and technical delivery decisions.

roleArchetypes.label: Software engineering
roleArchetypes.scope: Implements and verifies bounded software changes under repository authority.

roleArchetypes.label: Data/AI engineering
roleArchetypes.scope: Implements and evaluates bounded data/model/pipeline changes.

roleArchetypes.label: Platform/DevOps
roleArchetypes.scope: Provides environments, pipelines, platform controls, and deployment evidence.

roleArchetypes.label: Quality engineering
roleArchetypes.scope: Defines and executes test/quality evidence and traceability.

roleArchetypes.label: AI evaluation / TEVV
roleArchetypes.scope: Performs AI-specific test, evaluation, verification, and validation for bounded risks.

roleArchetypes.label: Release/change management
roleArchetypes.scope: Owns release/change authorization and controlled deployment coordination.

roleArchetypes.label: Service management
roleArchetypes.scope: Owns service governance, support model, and operational acceptance.

roleArchetypes.label: SRE/operations
roleArchetypes.scope: Operates, observes, responds, recovers, and supplies operational evidence.

roleArchetypes.label: Incident/recovery leadership
roleArchetypes.scope: Directs material incident, recovery, and continuity decisions.

roleArchetypes.label: Internal audit or independent assurance
roleArchetypes.scope: Independently assesses defined evidence for a bounded scope without becoming the delivery owner.

roleArchetypes.label: Affected-user/stakeholder representative
roleArchetypes.scope: Provides affected-user needs, impacts, challenge, and acceptance evidence where authorized.

participationLevels.label: Aware
participationLevels.evidenceRequirement: Can explain the relevant GAEP boundary and recognize when guided help is required.

participationLevels.label: Guided contributor
participationLevels.evidenceRequirement: Completes a bounded scenario with a named Practitioner observing and correcting decisions.

participationLevels.label: Practitioner
participationLevels.evidenceRequirement: Completes representative scenarios, handles failure/Unknown states, and produces reviewable evidence independently.

participationLevels.label: Assurer or accountable decision-maker
participationLevels.evidenceRequirement: Demonstrates challenge, escalation, authority-bound decision documentation, and independence where applicable.

participationLevels.label: Enterprise steward
participationLevels.evidenceRequirement: Maintains lifecycle policy, role separation, evidence quality, and cross-Initiative learning through scenario evidence.

competencyDimensions.label: GAEP lifecycle literacy
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Given a mixed current/target roadmap, identify executable checkpoints and non-executable target nodes without conflation.

competencyDimensions.label: Product and Initiative reasoning
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Bound a Product and change Initiative, state outcomes/exclusions, and identify a misleading scope assumption.

competencyDimensions.label: Domain and business analysis
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Derive business rules/events from evidence and keep disputed domain language unresolved.

competencyDimensions.label: Evidence and provenance
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Trace a candidate assertion to exact Source revision/locator and state its limitation.

competencyDimensions.label: Source governance
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Distinguish attachment, reviewed Source, Baseline, Provenance, change, and supersession decisions.

competencyDimensions.label: Candidate / accept / commit semantics
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Detect a changed candidate digest and refuse commit until exact re-review and acceptance.

competencyDimensions.label: Architecture and DDD
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Use DDD to reason about boundaries while selecting architecture style from evidence rather than assuming microservices.

competencyDimensions.label: Product Design
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Reconcile tool-neutral Product Design evidence and treat Figma as an optional adapter.

competencyDimensions.label: Backlog and requirements quality
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Trace a backlog slice to architecture decisions, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and target repository.

competencyDimensions.label: Testing and assurance
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Design tests/TEVV from risks and distinguish test evidence from independent assurance.

competencyDimensions.label: AI literacy and failure modes
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Identify hallucination, stale context, automation bias, and unsafe delegation in a candidate workflow.

competencyDimensions.label: Prompt/context governance
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Bound prompt context, sensitive data, model/provider, tool access, and retained audit evidence.

competencyDimensions.label: Security
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Threat-model an affected slice and connect mitigations to verification evidence without claiming security approval.

competencyDimensions.label: Privacy
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Identify purpose, data categories, minimization, rights, transfer, and unresolved privacy authority.

competencyDimensions.label: Risk and compliance
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Decide applicability, preserve residual risk, and route risk acceptance to the authorized role.

competencyDimensions.label: Repository governance
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Allocate a vertical slice across repositories and preserve merge/repository authority boundaries.

competencyDimensions.label: Delivery and release
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Separate implementation evidence, readiness, change authorization, release, and deployment decisions.

competencyDimensions.label: Operations, observability, incident, and recovery
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Use operational evidence to detect, respond, recover, learn, and feed a governed change back into Product work.

competencyDimensions.label: Auditability
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Reconstruct who decided what, from which exact evidence, under which scope and limitations.

competencyDimensions.label: Challenge, escalation, and decision documentation
competencyDimensions.scenarioEvidence: Challenge conflicting evidence, block unsafe progression, escalate to the right accountable role, and record disposition.

gatewayOutcomes.label: Ready for the selected bounded activity

gatewayRules: Assess only competencies required by the selected checkpoint/substep, role, and risk/applicability profile.
Use scenario evidence; self-confidence or job title alone is insufficient.
Do not calculate one universal competency score.
Competence does not grant authority; authority does not prove competence.
A regulated, high-risk, AI/data, security/privacy-material, release, or operations decision can require independent assurance even when participants are competent.
